content: Diphenhydramine is an antihistamine commonly used to alleviate symptoms associated with allergies, hay fever, and the common cold. These symptoms include rash, itching, watery eyes, itchy eyes/nose/throat, cough, runny nose, and sneezing. It is also effective in preventing and treating nausea, vomiting, and dizziness caused by motion sickness. The medication works by blocking histamine, a natural substance produced by the body during allergic reactions. Diphenhydramine is available in various forms, including tablets, capsules, liquids, and rapidly dissolving strips. It is important to follow the dosage instructions provided on the product packaging or as directed by a healthcare provider. For motion sickness prevention, the medication should be taken 30 minutes before travel or activity. To aid sleep, it should be taken approximately 30 minutes before bedtime. The dosage is determined based on factors such as age, medical condition, and response to treatment. This medication is not recommended for children under 6 years of age unless specifically directed by a doctor. Certain formulations, such as long-acting tablets or capsules, are not suitable for children under 12 years. Diphenhydramine does not cure or shorten the duration of the common cold and may cause serious side effects if misused. It should not be used to make a child sleepy or combined with other medications containing similar ingredients. Common side effects of diphenhydramine include drowsiness, dizziness, constipation, stomach upset, blurred vision, and dry mouth, nose, or throat. Older adults may be more sensitive to these effects, particularly drowsiness, dizziness, confusion, constipation, or difficulty urinating. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. If you experience severe symptoms such as passing out, trouble breathing, or seizures, seek immediate medical attention. Diphenhydramine may interact with other medications, potentially altering their effects or increasing the risk of side effects. It is important to inform your doctor or pharmacist about all medications and supplements you are taking. Avoid alcohol and other sedatives while using diphenhydramine, as they can enhance drowsiness and dizziness. Additionally, this medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as allergy skin tests, leading to inaccurate results. During pregnancy, diphenhydramine should only be used when clearly needed, as it passes into breast milk and may affect a nursing infant. It is contraindicated in premature infants, neonates, and nursing mothers. Diphenhydramine is considered a high-risk medication for elderly patients due to its potential to increase the risk of falls and its anticholinergic effects, which may exacerbate existing conditions such as benign prostatic hyperplasia or lower urinary tract issues. It is not recommended for treating insomnia in older adults, as tolerance develops and the risk of side effects increases. In case of overdose, symptoms may include severe drowsiness, seizures, or widened pupils. Immediate medical attention is required. Store diphenhydramine at room temperature, away from moisture and light, and keep it out of reach of children. Always consult your healthcare provider for guidance on the safe and effective use of this medication.
